title: Oracle Warns of More AI-Driven Layoffs After Cutting 21,000 Jobs in One Year
excerpt: The company's annual filing reveals it spent $1.84 billion on severance as it shed 13% of its workforce to fund a $55.7 billion AI data center buildout, with Indian teams among those impacted.
body:
• Oracle's workforce fell from 162,000 to 141,000 in fiscal 2026 — a 13% reduction — with the company explicitly citing AI adoption as a driver and warning of further cuts ahead.
  • Restructuring costs surged to $1.84 billion from $374 million a year earlier, as the company poured $55.7 billion into capital expenditures primarily for AI data center infrastructure.
  • Analysts project Oracle may need to cut another 10,000 to 15,000 positions to reach a sustainable cost structure, as it takes on roughly $50 billion in new debt to finance its AI ambitions.

Oracle's annual regulatory filing has put a concrete number behind months of rolling layoffs: the enterprise software giant shed 21,000 jobs over the past fiscal year, reducing its workforce from 162,000 to approximately 141,000 as of May 31, 2026. The cuts represent the largest single-year corporate workforce reduction in the tech sector this year.

In unusually direct language for a securities filing, Oracle tied the reductions to its AI strategy. "The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," the company stated in its 10-K report, adding ominously that it "may initiate new restructuring plans in the future."

The 6 A.M. Emails

The initial wave of layoffs in March drew attention not just for their scale but for how they were executed. Thousands of employees across the United States and India received termination emails at 6 a.m. Eastern from "Oracle Leadership," effective immediately. No prior conversation with managers preceded the notices, and system access was revoked shortly after, according to reports by MarketWatch and Fast Company.

"After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role."

— Oracle's termination email to employees, obtained by MarketWatch

The cuts hit hardest at Oracle Health — the $28.3 billion Cerner acquisition — where an estimated 8,000 to 10,000 positions were eliminated, according to Bloomberg and The Information. Cloud support teams, technical account managers covering pre-AI workloads, and ERP consulting divisions also took significant losses, while GPU operators, hardware engineers, and data center site reliability engineers were largely spared.

Funding the AI Buildout

The layoffs are inseparable from Oracle's massive pivot toward AI infrastructure. Capital expenditures hit $55.7 billion in fiscal 2026, driven primarily by data center construction. Oracle has taken on roughly $50 billion in new debt to finance an estimated $156 billion in total infrastructure commitments, anchored by a $300 billion, five-year cloud computing deal with OpenAI.

Operating lease commitments ballooned to $260 billion from $43.4 billion a year earlier — a roughly 500% increase — according to Jefferies analyst Brent Thill, who noted the commitments are "substantially all tied to data center arrangements" expected to run 15 to 19 years.

Oracle's Q3 earnings report had hinted at the restructuring weeks before the March cuts. "AI models for generating computer code have become so efficient that we have been restructuring our product development teams into smaller, more agile and productive groups," it said. "This new AI Code Generation technology is enabling us to build more software in less time with fewer people."

More Cuts Expected

Analysts at TD Cowen project Oracle may need to reduce its total workforce by up to 25%, suggesting another 10,000 to 15,000 positions could be eliminated before the restructuring is complete. The $1.84 billion restructuring charge — nearly five times the prior year's $374 million — reflects the intensity of the transformation.

Oracle's stock has struggled through the pivot. Shares have fallen about 12% this calendar year and sit roughly 48% below their September 2025 record high of $328.33.

"Oracle is the only Big Tech company executing a true zero-based-budgeting reset around AI. Microsoft is trimming. Meta is right-sizing after pandemic over-hiring. Oracle is fundamentally rebuilding its operating model around being a GPU landlord for OpenAI."

— Lisa Ellis, Senior Partner, MoffettNathanson

Impact on Indian Teams

Of the 21,000 jobs lost, approximately 12,000 were international positions. Oracle's India Development Centre was among the units affected, with employees in NetSuite, Oracle Health, and cloud support divisions reporting termination notices in the March wave, according to LinkedIn posts compiled by The Economic Times.

The tech industry's broader shift toward AI-funded layoffs has raised concerns among Indian IT professionals who make up a significant share of enterprise software workforces. Amazon cut 16,000 corporate roles in January, while Meta eliminated 8,000 positions and reassigned 7,000 people to AI-focused roles.

Oracle said it would "continually balance our resources and restructure our development group to help ensure we have the right people delivering the best cloud and AI products to our customers around the world."
